title: KCF Codegen Realization Report v1
description: The verdict of checking a realization manifest against the IR (and optionally the generated repository): whether every declared semantic identity is accounted for, and to what evidence level. `ok` means accounted (every identity has a disposition, realized ones cite artifacts, gaps are noted); `evidenceLevel` says how strongly it is grounded - `accounted` without --repo does NOT mean the artifacts exist.

repoChecked.description: Whether artifact/test paths and symbols were checked against a generated repository.

ok.description: Accounting holds: every IR identity has a disposition, realized ones cite artifacts, gaps are noted. This is NOT proof the code exists or is correct - see evidenceLevel.

evidenceLevel.description: Strongest evidence established: none (accounting failed) < accounted (declared, not checked against a repo) < artifact-verified (files exist) < symbol-verified (named symbols found) < test-present (test files exist). Higher levels (test-executed, behavior-verified) require an execution harness this structural verifier does not run.

byClass.description: Per-construct-class realization ratio (realized vs total accounted). Distinguishes an implementation from a scaffold that accounts for every identity but realizes none of a behavioural class (e.g. rules, invoke actions).

notices.description: Non-fatal observations - notably a construct class that is 0% realized (accounted for but entirely delegated/deferred), which is almost always worth a human look. Reporting only; it does not fail the build (a frontend-only tier legitimately delegates persistence).

positionUnstableIdentities.description: Identities assigned a position-based `section#index` fallback (the item declared no qualifiedName/id/name). Accounted for, but NOT stable across reordering/versions - a durable manifest should give these items a stable id.
